discovery: Fluctuation theorems and exact work relations for systems driven far from equilibrium

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

subfield: Statistical physics / non-equilibrium and quantum thermodynamics
motivation: For more than a century, the second law was an inequality valid only on average and near equilibrium. Evans and co-workers (1993-94) discovered that the probability of entropy-consuming fluctuations obeys an exact exponential symmetry. Jarzynski (1997) showed that equilibrium free-energy differences follow exactly from work done in arbitrarily fast, irreversible processes, and Crooks (1998-99) unified these into a detailed fluctuation theorem relating forward and time-reversed path probabilities. These results are rare in physics: exact, general equalities that hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium, across classical and quantum platforms. They have been verified quantitatively in single-molecule pulling, colloidal traps, single-electron boxes and trapped ions, and are routinely used to extract free energies. They founded stochastic and quantum thermodynamics, underpinning today's thermodynamic uncertainty relations, bounds on the precision and efficiency of nanoscale engines, and the energetics of quantum information processing.
